title: Why do airlines charge different prices for the same seat?
sources: MIT International Center for Air Transportation Revenue Management

lines.text: On a commercial flight, the passenger sitting directly next to you in economy might have paid half your ticket price.
lines.caps: Why does the person *next to you | pay half your *flight?

lines.text: Airlines pioneered dynamic yield management algorithms to squeeze maximum revenue from every single seat.
A flight's seats are divided into invisible pricing tiers called fare buckets.
lines.caps: Seats are divided into *invisible | fare pricing *buckets

lines.text: Early leisure travelers book cheap bucket seats months ahead of time.
As departure day nears, remaining seats shift into corporate business buckets priced three times higher.
lines.caps: Last-minute seats shift to *expensive | corporate *business tiers!

lines.text: Algorithms update prices thousands of times a day based on route searches, fuel prices, and competitor inventory.
lines.caps: Algorithms adjust fares *thousands | of times per *day

lines.text: The best sweet spot for domestic flight prices is typically one to three months before takeoff.
lines.caps: Book 1 to 3 months *ahead | for the lowest airfare *prices!
